forces.title: Massive data center expansion drives networking equipment demand
forces.description: The anticipated surge in data center capital expenditures, driven by AI compute, globally and in India, will significantly boost demand for communications and networking equipment. US hyperscalers plan ~US$1 trillion for AI infrastructure in 2027, while India's data center capacity is set to grow from ~1.9 GW in FY26 to add ~4.5 GW over the next five years. This sustained growth underpins strong demand for routers, switches, optical networking, and associated hardware.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

forces.title: Government funding for 5G/6G and quantum communications projects
forces.description: India has allocated significant funding to projects spanning emerging telecommunications technologies such as 5G/6G, AI, and quantum communications. 136 projects received Rs. 550 crore (US$ 57.82 million) in funding as of December 2025. This direct government support and investment in advanced telecom infrastructure will act as a major tailwind for RAN hardware manufacturers and other companies producing physical equipment for transmitting data in these next-generation networks.

forces.title: Increased IT spending in India supports hardware and networking
forces.description: India’s IT spending is expected to reach US$ 176.3 billion (Rs. 15,50,734 crore) in 2026, driven by data center expansion and AI-enabled software investments. This substantial increase in domestic IT expenditure directly benefits the Communications & Networking Equipment sub-industry by fueling demand for enterprise networking hardware (routers, switches, wireless AP) and optical networking solutions, essential for supporting expanded IT infrastructure and advanced digital services.
forces.source_title: Information Technology And BPM Industry In India

forces.title: Evolution to AI-centric data centers demanding higher performance equipment
forces.description: The nature of data consumption and workloads in data centers is fundamentally changing, shifting from traditional enterprise applications to compute-intensive tasks like AI model training and real-time analytics. This evolution demands higher rack densities, more resilient power architectures, and advanced cooling solutions, redefining data center design. Consequently, there is a structural shift towards more sophisticated and high-performance networking equipment, including optical networking, to handle increased data flow and low-latency requirements.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

forces.title: Strong increase in internet connections boosts networking infrastructure demand
forces.description: Internet connections in India surpassed 100 crore in June 2025, a nearly 300% increase since March 2014. This rapid and sustained growth in internet adoption across the country creates a significant tailwind for the Communications & Networking Equipment sector. It drives the need for expanded and upgraded physical equipment for transmitting data, including enterprise networking hardware, optical networking, and RAN hardware to support the burgeoning user base and data traffic.

forces.title: India’s emerging role as APAC data center hub drives subsea connectivity
forces.description: India's emergence as a prominent data center hub for the Asia Pacific region, supported by improving infrastructure, will strengthen its role for regional traffic flows. This includes enhanced subsea connectivity, which is critical for international data transmission. The continuous improvement and expansion of subsea cable networks directly translates to increased demand for specialized optical networking equipment to handle growing cross-border data traffic, offering a significant upside for manufacturers.
forces.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

forces.title: Domestic policy support for electronics component manufacturing
forces.description: The expansion of the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) with a US$ 4.53 billion outlay in Union Budget 2026–27 aims to strengthen domestic supply chains for chips and components. These components account for a large share of India’s electronics imports. This policy push can lead to greater localization in the supply of critical inputs for communications and networking equipment, reducing import dependency and fostering domestic production capabilities within IN080303.

forces.title: Long lead times and supply chain constraints for key components
forces.description: The rapid reindustrialization in the US, especially in AI compute and power infrastructure, faces critical bottlenecks in supply chains, with long lead times for key components. While this is noted for US manufacturers, it indicates potential global supply chain pressures that could impact the availability and cost of critical inputs for communications and networking equipment manufacturers in India, leading to delays or higher production costs for IN080303.

forces.title: Geopolitical disruption risk from concentrated semiconductor supply
forces.description: Over 90% of leading-edge chips are produced in Taiwan, making the global AI compute sector vulnerable to potential disruption from geopolitical tensions. Since networking equipment, particularly for high-performance data centers and AI infrastructure, relies heavily on leading-edge chips, any such disruption could severely impact the supply, cost, and innovation timelines for IN080303, posing a significant risk to manufacturing and deployment schedules.

forces.title: AI adoption driving innovation in networking/photonics solutions
forces.description: The need to sustain cost reductions for AI inference, requiring three to four orders of magnitude drop, is driving innovation across various technology domains, including networking/photonics. Companies are announcing road maps for these areas to improve efficiency. This innovation push for advanced networking and optical solutions, especially those integrated with AI infrastructure, presents a significant upside for the IN080303 sector to develop and market next-generation physical equipment for data transmission.
forces.source_title: The $2.3 trillion horizon: How AI is rewriting the semiconductor story

viewpoints.title: India poised as prominent APAC data center hub, driving connectivity equipment demand
viewpoints.description: India is rapidly emerging as a prominent data center hub for the Asia Pacific region, overtaking markets like Hong Kong, Singapore, and Tokyo that face land and power constraints. India offers scale, cost efficiency, and large domestic demand, attracting long-term infrastructure investments. As subsea connectivity and regional traffic increase, India's role as a hub for South Asia, the Middle East, and parts of Southeast Asia will strengthen, leading to robust demand for optical networking and data transmission equipment.
viewpoints.source_title: India data centre opportunity - From emerging demand hub to integrated data centre powerhouse

viewpoints.title: US data center growth to sustain strong demand for networking equipment through 2035
viewpoints.description: Despite some market uncertainties, the risk of overbuilding data center power infrastructure in the US is low, with demand for AI compute expected to last. Data center IT load, which includes networking equipment, is projected to grow approximately 27 percent annually through 2030, reaching 121 GW, and a sevenfold increase by 2035 in the continued-momentum scenario. This sustained expansion ensures durable, committed growth for networking equipment providers.
viewpoints.source_title: Powering AI: How real is the risk of overbuilding?

viewpoints.title: Government initiatives to boost domestic electronics manufacturing, including networking hardware
viewpoints.description: The Indian government's 'Digital India' and 'Make in India' initiatives, coupled with a favorable FDI Policy, are simplifying the establishment of manufacturing units across the country. Programs like the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes and the Electronics Components Manufacturing Scheme (ECMS) with an outlay of US$ 4.53 billion are strengthening domestic supply chains for chips and components. This creates a supportive environment for localizing the production of communications and networking equipment and related components.

demand_drivers.driver: Global Data Center & IT Spending Surge
demand_drivers.description: Global IT expenditure is forecast to hit US$ 6.15 trillion in 2026, a 10.8% rise from 2025. Overall data center spending is projected to climb 31.7%, exceeding US$ 650 billion in 2026, compared with almost US$ 500 billion the prior year. This massive spending on IT and data centers directly translates to high demand for networking equipment (routers, switches, optical networking) to enable connectivity and data flow within these facilities.

India's data center market size is projected to increase from ~USD1.7 billion in FY26 to ~USD6.8 billion by FY30, reflecting a rapid expansion. The country's installed data center capacity has more than tripled since FY19, reaching ~1.9 GW in FY26, with a development pipeline expected to add ~4.5 GW over the next five years. This significant build-out directly fuels demand for enterprise networking hardware and optical networking solutions.

The current data center growth cycle is increasingly driven by hyperscale cloud providers, global content platforms, and AI-first companies. Compute-intensive workloads like AI model training, real-time analytics, and video streaming demand higher rack densities, more resilient power architectures, and advanced cooling solutions, fundamentally redefining data center design. This requires advanced and higher-capacity networking equipment.

136 projects with a total cost of Rs. 550 crore (US$ 57.82 million) have received funding, spanning emerging telecommunications technologies such as 5G/6G, AI, and quantum communications. The rollout and development of these next-generation mobile networks (5G/6G) necessitate significant investments in RAN hardware and optical networking equipment for backhaul and core networks.

Internet connections in India surpassed the 100 crore milestone in June 2025, reaching 100.29 crore, representing a growth of 298.77% since March 2014. Rapid digitalization across consumer and enterprise segments, coupled with affordable smartphones and low-cost data tariffs, drives increased data consumption, which in turn necessitates robust and expanded networking infrastructure.

India's data center growth is supported by an increasing infrastructure network, including multiple international subsea cable landing stations and expanding fiber networks. This strengthens domestic and international connectivity, driving demand for optical networking equipment for both backbone and last-mile connections, supporting the physical transmission of data.

new_opportunities.description: Multiple global players are investing in India-based manufacturing for racks, cooling, and power systems for data centers. This trend, coupled with incentives like duty-free SEZ imports, could extend to localized manufacturing of networking equipment and components, reducing lead times and costs, and positioning India as a regional supplier.
new_opportunities.opportunity: Domestic Manufacturing for Data Center Components

new_opportunities.description: The shift towards compute-intensive workloads like AI model training demands higher rack densities and more resilient power architectures within data centers. This creates an opportunity for providers of advanced networking hardware with higher bandwidth, lower latency, and enhanced integration capabilities to support these specialized, high-performance computing environments.

market_sizing.methodology: Analysis of data center expansion and IT spending forecasts globally and in India, identifying key demand drivers for networking equipment.
